clue.text: Down to earth deliveries

parts.note: reads like modest, practical shipments, but means supplies literally dropped down to the ground from an aircraft

explanation.surface: A no-nonsense courier service praised for its sensible deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down to earth' looks like 'sensible', but here it means the goods come down from the sky to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Packages parachuted from a plane are delivered from the air down to the ground.

clue.text: Decided jointly on a silver oboe

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an oboe is a double-reed woodwind, so a reed instrument stands for it

explanation.surface: A musical pair settle together on buying a silver oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling something by mutual consent is reaching a shared decision.

clue.text: The severity of weather could mean he set the sails, it's said

indicators.note: the clue says the word is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the description

parts.note: a rigger is a sailor who fits a ship's rigging and sails

explanation.surface: Harsh weather conditions demand a sailor who knows how to set sails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could mean' joins the definition to the wordplay; RIGGER and RIGOUR sound alike in a British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: We speak of the rigours of a harsh climate, meaning its harshness.

clue.text: Enjoy the taste of ketchup

definitions.meaning: a tomato sauce is a kind of condiment or pickle eaten with food

explanation.surface: Someone savouring the flavour of tomato sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means savour with pleasure; the noun is a sauce or chutney served with food, such as ketchup.

clue.text: Way one brief cigarette works at producing disease

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: in the sense of 'works at' or ferments, these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
cig is the short form of cigarette

explanation.surface: Smoking a cigarette on the way is how one catches an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a verb about the cigarette's effect, but it is the anagram signal; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that causes illness, such as a germ or virus, is described this way.

clue.text: Cope with lover on date

parts.note: a woman's man is her lover or partner
a date can be a period or era, as an age is

explanation.surface: Someone getting by with a romantic partner on an evening out.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle or deal with a situation successfully.

clue.text: Hides from a science graduate and various dons

parts.note: BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree

indicators.note: various means differing in arrangement, so the letters of dons are put in another order

explanation.surface: A scientist hides from several university lecturers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges DONS to make CONDS (a rearrangement).
explanation.definitionFit: To flee secretly, slipping away from the people who would hold you.

clue.text: A classic way to sort out the high fliers

parts.note: via is Latin, a classical language, for road or way

indicators.note: out signals the letters of sort are put out of order

explanation.surface: Advice on how to sort out top achievers in the traditional way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SORT into TORS; 'to' is a link. The high fliers are literal pilots, not achievers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots are people who fly aircraft, so they are high fliers in a literal sense.

clue.text: Jewels without love are seldom transferred

indicators.note: transferred means moved about, so the remaining letters change places
without tells us to remove a piece from the letters before they are shuffled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: Gems passed on rarely once love has gone from a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O (love) from ARE SELDOM, then 'transferred' rearranges the remaining letters ARESELDM.
explanation.definitionFit: Green gemstones of the beryl family are prized precious stones.

clue.text: Put restrictions on use of gun brought back with a note

indicators.note: brought back means the word for the gun is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Lawmakers bring back firearm rules alongside an official note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns LUGER into REGUL; 'use of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To control by rules, limiting what may be done.

clue.text: Aim to praise the modification

indicators.note: a modification is a change, so the letters of praise are changed in order

explanation.surface: An instruction to praise a change someone has made.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim at something is to strive or hope to reach it.

clue.text: Paint a bird and some wandering lions

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

indicators.note: wandering means moving about, so the letters of lions roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A picture of a bird among some lions on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-based household paint used on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: Go back and start sorting out some of the stages

indicators.note: go back means read the letters in the reverse direction
some of means only part of the run of letters is taken from the words

explanation.surface: An instruction to retreat and begin tidying up some theatre stages.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ARTSOR sit inside 'stART SORting'; 'Go back' turns them round. 'out' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised platforms for speakers are plural of a Latin word for a platform.

clue.text: General office worker female, needs fellow to sort out diary

parts.note: a girl is a female
F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: to sort out means put in order, so the letters of diary are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office worker who is a woman needs a man to organise her diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sort out' rearranges DIARY into RIDAY; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-purpose assistant, named after Robinson Crusoe's servant Friday, who handles general office tasks.

clue.text: Confused Oscar in exhortation to show revolutionary feelings

indicators.note: in tells us the playwright is placed inside the command

parts.note: red is the colour of revolution, so the urging is 'be red!'
Oscar Wilde, the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Someone puzzled by a call to express revolutionary passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the NATO alphabet's O, but it is the playwright, set inside the cry 'Be red!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Perplexed and unable to understand, as a puzzled person is.

clue.text: Feeling poorly, he is in bad form

indicators.note: is in tells us the following pieces go inside the word for bad

parts.note: feeling poorly means ill or unwell

explanation.surface: A man is unwell and therefore out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like condition or fitness, but it is a printed form with a firm's name at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed sheet headed with a business's name and address, used for invoices.

clue.text: They learn from seeing the London Symphony Orchestra crash out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: LSO is the usual abbreviation for the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Students learn from watching the orchestra collapse during a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LSO with CRASH; 'from seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned people or students devote themselves to study.

clue.text: Put off accepting tin container

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: Someone postpones accepting a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.

clue.text: Fit for the consumer after 50% increase? That's unbelievable

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first
fifty per cent means half, here the first half of the word increase

parts.note: edible means fit to be eaten

explanation.surface: Food made safe to eat after a fifty per cent price hike, which shoppers find hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: '50%' takes the first half of the word increase; 'Fit for the consumer' means safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief or amazement uses this adjective, meaning hard to credit.

clue.text: When son is first to help

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A child is the first to lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or support someone in a task.

clue.text: Sound doubtful in time, but go along with it

indicators.note: in places the hesitation sound inside the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
um is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates for a while but then agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone, agreeing with them to keep them happy.

clue.text: Perhaps his age works on an entertainer

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer feels the effects of growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' and 'on' are links; 'works' rearranges HIS AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation to entertain guests.

clue.text: With which to scrub the lavatory, originally filthy and horrendous

parts.note: loo is a British informal word for the lavatory

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Cleaning a dirty and frightful toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd fibre used as a bath sponge for scrubbing the skin.

clue.text: Newspapermen rue the outcome of undue influence

parts.note: the press is the collective term for journalists

indicators.note: an outcome is what something turns into, so the letters of rue come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Journalists regret the result of improper persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the outcome of' rearranges RUE into URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coercion or forceful persuasion applied to someone to make them act.

clue.text: Speaks highly of vote made in reform slate

indicators.note: made in tells us the cross goes inside the rearranged letters
reform means reshape, so the letters of slate are reshaped

parts.note: a cross, X, is marked on a ballot paper to vote

explanation.surface: Praise for a ballot cast on a reformed list of candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges SLATE; X goes inside to make EXALTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise or glorify someone extravagantly.

clue.text: They recommend present day face masks

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of the calendar
visors are shields worn over the face

explanation.surface: Modern face masks are advised by experts.
explanation.definitionFit: Consultants give advice and suggest courses of action.

clue.text: Want to remove father?

parts.note: the prefix de- means remove, as in de-ice
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A question whether one wishes to get rid of one's father.
explanation.walkthrough: The query flags that DE- is a prefix meaning 'take away' rather than a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for or wish for something.

clue.text: Emotional instability could be treated this year

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mental disorder that might be cured within the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link; 'treated' rearranges THIS YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncontrolled emotion or excitement, as in a frenzy.
